title: Migrate FastAPI to Go
bottom_line: Run one command inside a fastapi-template project and Claude rewrites it in Go on its own branch, keeping routes, pages and logins, then removes Python.

sections.heading: Run one command inside your FastAPI project

before.label: You start with
before.text: A project scaffolded with `fastapi-template`: FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLModel/Alembic, fastapi-cache2, OpenRouter and signed cookies, all in Python.

after.label: You end with
after.text: The same project on the `go-webapp-template` stack (net/http, html/template, pgx/goose, go-redis, slog), in the same repository, with Python deleted at the end.

blocks.caption: Python is deleted only after the Go build passes every gate.

cards.title: Type the command
cards.text: `/go-webapp-template:fastapi-go-migration`, optionally with `--branch <name>` to work on a branch other than `go-migration`.

cards.title: Just ask
cards.text: Say "migrate this app to Go" inside the project.

blocks.text: This is the second skill of the go-webapp-template plugin. Claude also uses it on its own when you want to move, port, convert, rewrite or migrate a Python/FastAPI backend to Go or golang, even without naming either template.
It also starts when you say "replace FastAPI with Go", "rewrite the backend in Go", "fastapi to go" or "make this a Go app", or ask what it would take to drop Python from a web app.

blocks.title: Not for
items: Scaffolding a brand-new Go app. Use go-webapp-template for that.

sections.heading: Everything users see stays the same

rows: Every page address the Python app had exists in the Go app.
The same pages, converted from Jinja2 to Go's `html/template`.
Existing sessions survive, so logged-in users stay logged in.

terms.definition: A page or address the app answers, such as `/` or a form's target.
A file that changes the database structure. Alembic runs them in Python; goose runs them in Go.
One goose migration that describes the whole existing database.
A check that must pass before Python is removed.
The final switch: Python is deleted and deploys run the Go program.
End-to-end tests that drive the running app like a user would, through a browser (Playwright).

blocks.title: Decisions already made (Claude does not ask about these)
items: The work happens in place, on a `go-migration` branch, or the name you give with `--branch <name>`. Nothing is committed without your ok, and nothing is deployed by the skill.

Alembic is replaced by one idempotent goose baseline: a no-op on the production database Alembic already migrated, and a full schema on a fresh one. The `alembic_version` table stays until a later migration drops it.
Python Playwright e2e tests under `tests/` are kept (they are black-box HTTP tests) and pointed at the Go binary. They are the only Python left, so `uv` stays for them.
Python unit tests are ported to Go or deleted, file by file.

sections.heading: Have Go, uv, Postgres and a clean git tree ready

cards.title: Go 1.22 or newer
cards.text: Checked with `go version`. If Go is missing, Claude tells you how to install it and stops.

cards.title: uv
cards.text: The Python package tool. It stays after the migration for the e2e tests.

cards.title: A reachable Postgres
cards.text: `psql` or a Docker Postgres Claude can reach, needed to prove the baseline.

cards.title: Redis
cards.text: Reachable, if the app uses it.

cards.title: Clean git status
cards.text: `git status` must be clean. Claude creates or switches to the `go-migration` branch.

cards.title: plan-tools for big repos
cards.text: The skill uses the plan-tools plugin for big repos. If it is missing, Claude asks you to install it and waits.

blocks.title: It stops if this is not a fastapi-template project
blocks.text: Claude first confirms the project has the fastapi-template shape: `app/__init__.py` with `_assert_env`, `app/main.py`, `alembic/` and `pyproject.toml`. If not, it says so and stops.

It also reads the project's `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `Procfile` / `start.sh`, `Makefile`, CI workflows, `tests/conftest.py`, `.env.example`, `scripts/worktree_env.py` and `.claude/settings.json`, because these say how the app is actually run and deployed.

sections.heading: The migration runs in six phases

steps.title: Inventory
steps.text: Lists every route, model, Jinja construct, custom filter, env var, grown feature (arq, OAuth, email, …), and how tests and deploy start the app. Written to `.planning/inventory.md` so later sessions never need the Python source wholesale.

steps.title: Baseline migration
steps.text: Writes `migrations/00001_baseline.sql` from the SQLModel metadata with `CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS`: a no-op on the production database Alembic already migrated, a full schema on a fresh one. Its `Down` part is intentionally empty.

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: Writes `.planning/SPEC.md`: sessions per router group, Go functions for custom filters (a FuncMap), a cookie-signer check, and which unit tests to port or delete. Every feature with no Go counterpart is resolved with you in one question.

steps.title: Port
steps.text: Session by session: database code (`internal/db/<table>.go`), then handlers, then templates (Jinja2 to `html/template`). After each session it runs `go build/vet/test` and a Python-vs-Go route parity check.

steps.title: Gates
steps.text: Route parity, a cookie test (existing sessions survive), every page rendered with `missingkey=error`, the baseline applied twice, and the e2e suite green against the Go binary.

steps.title: Cutover
steps.text: Rewrites `tests/conftest.py` to run `./out`, carries per-worktree port/DB/Redis isolation over to Go (keeping an existing Python script's slot key, ports and DB names), makes `pyproject.toml` tests-only, adds `railpack.json`, deletes `app/` and `alembic/`, updates CI, README and CLAUDE.md, and prints the deploy checklist.

blocks.title: Files it writes for you to read
blocks.text: `.planning/inventory.md` (what must be ported), `.planning/SPEC.md` (the plan and your answers), `migrations/00001_baseline.sql` (the database baseline) and `.planning/progress.md` (progress and gate results).

blocks.title: Why railpack.json
blocks.text: It names the Go provider plus an explicit `./cmd/server` build command, so Railway neither picks Python nor builds the root `embed.go` package.

cards.title: 3 routers or fewer
cards.text: With no grown features, one run works through the sessions in order.

cards.title: Anything bigger
cards.text: More than 3 routers, or any grown feature: the plan is split into sessions with the plan-tools plugin (`plan-tools:split-plan`).

points.text: Progress lives in `.planning/progress.md` and in the repo itself, so any later session can resume.

sections.heading: Claude stops and asks you before these decisions

cards.title: Features without a Go match
cards.text: numpy/pandas, websockets, i18n, HEIC/WebP encoding, MCP OAuth server, long-lived arq jobs. All such questions come in one round.

cards.title: Changed cookie signer
cards.text: If `app/utils.py` signs cookies differently from the template and the project has live users, Claude confirms the port before touching sessions.

cards.title: Timed links in flight
cards.text: `itsdangerous` timed links (email verification, unsubscribe): replicate their format or invalidate them.

cards.title: Commits
cards.text: It commits at the end of a session only if you said commits are pre-approved for the branch; otherwise it stops and asks once for the whole branch.

cards.title: Production and Railway
cards.text: Anything that touches the production database or Railway.

sections.heading: Nine gates must pass before Python is removed

items.label: gates before cutover
items.note: a failed gate is fixed and re-run, never skipped

rows: every Python route exists in Go
a browser with a Python-era cookie is still logged in on the Go server
every page renders with `missingkey=error`, with no blank spots
applied twice to a scratch database; no-op on a prod-schema copy; `./out migrate status` shows it
every column with a Python-side default is supplied in the Go `INSERT`/`UPDATE`
`uv run pytest tests` green against the Go binary; collected test count unchanged
each answer you gave is implemented as recorded in SPEC.md
`make dev`; log in, hit each top-level page, one HTMX fragment, one form post

sections.heading: You deploy it; the skill only prints the checklist

nodes.label: You set pre-deploy
nodes.note: `./out migrate up` in the Railway dashboard.

nodes.label: First deploy migrates
nodes.note: The pre-deploy command runs the migration.

items: The skill never deploys and never touches the production database.
It does not run `migrate up` against production itself. The first deploy does, via the pre-deploy command you set in the Railway dashboard.
Nothing is committed without your ok.

next_action.text: Open your fastapi-template project with a clean git status and type `/go-webapp-template:fastapi-go-migration`.
next_action.detail: Claude first checks the project shape, creates or switches to the `go-migration` branch, then checks your tools.
